$comment: The mutation-arm registry. Every `@:killer('<name>')` in the test tree
resolves to a `name` below or the build stops; every arm below is named by
at least one `@:killer` or the build stops; and every `type`/`method` below
has to still exist or the build stops. Run one with
`tools/mutation-arm.sh <NAME>`, all of them with `--all`.
An arm cuts exactly one way. `force` inserts `return <force>;` directly
after the member's signature, leaving the rest of the body behind as dead
code — the shape S94 measured 22 of. `find`/`replace` splices text inside
the member instead, for a cut a constant cannot express; both are
`hxq patch --select '<kind>:<method>'` payloads, so an arm survives every
edit that does not rename its member, which a stored line number does not.
`find` and `replace` are each ONE string or a LIST of them, of equal
length — N pairs applied in a single `hxq patch` payload, which alternates
old / new sections. Every pair is located against the ORIGINAL member text,
so the list is order-independent and a pair may not be written against
another pair's output. Reach for it when the cut is two disjoint edits: one
pair would have to widen its fragment until it bridges them, and a cut that
MOVES a statement cannot be written as one pair at all.
`kind` is the projected node the selector addresses and defaults to
`FnMember`. A grammar DECLARATION has no method to cut — its `@:re`
terminal is a module-level `MetaCall` — so such an arm spells its kind and
is answered by the parser (`unit.MutationArmAddressTest`) rather than by
the typer. Only `find`/`replace` can carry one: a forced `return` is
spliced after a function signature.

arms.name: M-ADDRESS-NO-ROOT-ANCHOR
arms.note: the root-anchored last attempt is dropped, so a node hanging directly off the module has no named ancestor to widen to and falls back to an --nth ordinal - the depth `>>` cannot express and no listing then spells

arms.name: M-ADMITS-TRUE
arms.note: every write is admitted whatever half of the scope recorded it, so a third-party write to a field NAME poisons a project candidate again

arms.name: M-ALWAYS-NEXT
arms.note: every value of sameLine.comprehensionFor becomes `next`, so a body the key asked to keep on the head line leaves it

arms.name: M-ALWAYS-SAME
arms.note: every value of sameLine.comprehensionFor becomes `same`, so `keep` stops reproducing the source break

arms.name: M-ARM-ANYNAME
arms.note: arm lookup answers the first declared arm for every name, so an undeclared @:killer resolves and the build-time refusal is gone

arms.name: M-ARM-ROW-OK
arms.note: per-row validation reports nothing, so an arm declaring neither cut — or both — is accepted

arms.name: M-BINDER-KINDS-PARAMS-ONLY
arms.note: the named-binder vocabulary collapses to the parameter slots, so a local declaration, a local function, a catch variable, a loop iterator and a case binder all stop binding their own name - a backing-field reference re-binds to whichever one shadows it and the rename rewrites it anyway

arms.name: M-BUILDMACRO-TRUE
arms.note: every type reads as carrying a build macro, so static-constant stops promoting a field a macro cannot have written

arms.name: M-CLAIM-ALL-RECORDED
arms.note: every prose claim reads as already recorded by an annotation, so the census empties and the ratchet has nothing to compare

arms.name: M-CLAIM-CODE-BLIND
arms.note: the code senses of `control` stay in the text, so a rule's doc about control flow reads as a fixture claiming to be a control

arms.name: M-CLAIM-NEG-BLIND
arms.note: `NOT killed by` stays in the text, so the one fixture that says it has no arm reads as claiming one

arms.name: M-CLAIM-NOKINDS
arms.note: no doc comment claims anything, so the census is empty and every prose convention reads as already annotated

arms.name: M-CLAIM-RAW-DOC
arms.note: the doc keeps its gutter and line breaks, so a claim wrapped across two lines is invisible — the failure mode of a line-oriented search

arms.name: M-CLI-UNKNOWN-NO-PLURAL-PROBE
arms.find: return direct.length > 0 || !name.endsWith('s') ? direct : CliWalk.findFuzzy(name.substr(0, name.length - 1), pool);
arms.note: the singular-stem retry is dropped, so `apq members` is five edits and no substring away from every real command and the unknown-subcommand notice offers nothing - the exact miss the notice replaced the whole help page to answer

arms.name: M-COND-FRAME-CONDITION-RAW
arms.note: a branch key is the condition's raw bytes, so `#if (js)` and `#if js` stop comparing equal and two sibling regions guarding one build read as different branches again

arms.name: M-COND-FRAME-REGION-KEYED
arms.find: for (i in 0...a.length) if (a[i].branch != b[i].branch || a[i].condition != b[i].condition) return false;
arms.replace: for (i in 0...a.length) if (a[i].region != b[i].region || a[i].branch != b[i].branch) return false;
arms.note: two positions are the same branch only when they sit in the same region OCCURRENCE, so `#if a f #end #if a f #end` reads as two branches and `remove-member` deletes both declarations of a pair no build can compile

arms.name: M-COND-GAP-KEEPS-DIRECTIVES
arms.note: the mention scan reads a raw region's own directives again, so renaming a local `debug` beside `#if debug` - or one named `end` beside the region's `#end` - is refused by the directive that guards it

arms.name: M-COND-GAP-SCANS-NOTHING
arms.note: no byte of a raw region is scanned at all, so the fail-closed gate stops seeing every occurrence it exists to see and every name-driven op rewrites around such a region in silence

arms.name: M-CUDDLE-FLATONLY
arms.note: restores the pre-S146 gate — only an item that CANNOT render flat cuddles, so a comprehension that renders flat and still overflows keeps its `[` on a line of its own

arms.name: M-CUDDLE-FALLBACK-INDENT
arms.find: final item: Null<Doc> = itemFlat < 0 ? items[0] : dropComprehensionBody(items[0]);
arms.replace: final item: Null<Doc> = itemFlat < 0 ? items[0] : cols + itemFlat <= lineWidth ? null : dropComprehensionBody(items[0]);
arms.note: restores the S146 threshold — a flat item that fits the line `shapeOnePerLine` would give it keeps its own bracket line, so a comprehension whose item fits one indent deeper but not after `[ ` is refused the cuddle (T674)

arms.name: M-CUDDLE-OFF
arms.note: the comprehension cuddled-open shape never fires, so `[ for (…)` goes back to its own bracket line

arms.name: M-DECLARINGFILES-EMPTY
arms.note: no type is declared anywhere, so a check that resolves a simple name to its declaring file stops seeing it

arms.name: M-DECLSITE-SCOPEWIDE
arms.note: the owner-file pin is gone, so a declaration range comes only from the scope-wide simple name and a type sharing one with a library type has none

arms.name: M-ELSE-GATE
arms.note: restores the S76 veto S78 removed — a comprehension whose body is an if/else refuses to cuddle its `[` again

arms.name: M-EMPTY-B-ANY-NONEMPTY
arms.find: loop is redundant only for a SINGLE-CHARACTER $search — '
arms.replace: loop is redundant for any non-empty $search — '
arms.note: the empty-B message claims the single call does the same work for every non-empty S again, which 'aabb'.replace('ab', '') == 'ab' refutes

arms.name: M-FANOUT-FIRST
arms.note: the specific comprehensionFor key is read BEFORE the general expressionIf fanout, so the fanout clobbers it — the S77 precedence PERMUTED, which is what its note asked for and what one find/replace pair could not express

arms.name: M-FIRST-LINE-FIT
arms.note: FitLine goes back to placing a body by its FIRST line, so a body that cannot render flat glues to the head line again

arms.name: M-STRICT-HEAD-DELIM-OFF
arms.note: restores the blanket refusal, so an expression-`for` whose body is a keyword-led construct opening a delimiter leaves the head line again

arms.name: M-FN-SCOPE-KINDS-DROPS-METHODS
arms.note: the METHOD half of the scope vocabulary is dropped and only the function VALUES remain, so a method body stops counting as a scope that can bind the property name and the `this.` qualifier a shadowed reference needs is never emitted

arms.name: M-FN-SCOPE-KINDS-FROZEN
arms.note: the derivation is frozen back into the hand copy it replaced - identical for the Haxe grammar and blind to every other, which is exactly the state the census is retiring

arms.name: M-HASSUBTYPE-FALSE
arms.note: no type has a subtype, so prefer-enum-abstract stops refusing a container something extends

arms.name: M-INHERITS-FALSE
arms.note: no member reads as inherited, so redundant-this stops flagging a `this.` on a base-declared member

arms.name: M-ISSUBTYPE-FALSE
arms.note: the subtype relation is empty, so redundant-upcast and unreachable-catch stop seeing the relation they report on

arms.name: M-KINDS
arms.note: CONTAINER_PLAIN collapses into NONE, so the generated forwarder and the classifier stop agreeing on the four codes

arms.name: M-LACKSMEMBER-FALSE
arms.note: no absence is ever provable, so field-init-in-constructor stops ranking a constant it could prove nothing about

arms.name: M-LINT-BASELINE-NO-SUBTRACTION
arms.note: the multiset subtraction is gone, so every standing finding comes back as new and `--baseline` degrades to the whole-file dump it exists to replace - silently, since a delta that is too LARGE still reads as a delta

arms.name: M-LINT-FIX-CENSUS-UNGATED
arms.note: the zero-edit gate is dropped, so a `--fix` run that wrote nothing prints the whole per-rule accounting about it again - ~1450 bytes of stderr per write op, which is what the slice measured and removed

arms.name: M-MEMO-OFF
arms.note: the project index is rebuilt on every demand, so the two field rules pay for it once each per pass instead of sharing one

arms.name: M-NAME-CLASH-KINDS-NO-BINDERS
arms.note: the binder half of the ambiguity vocabulary is dropped, so a second local function of the same name no longer clashes and the local-function call set is proven complete while carrying another function's calls

arms.name: M-NAMEOUTSIDE-TRUE
arms.note: every name reads as occurring outside its own file, so unused-public-member keeps every member it should have flagged

arms.name: M-NO-INVALIDATE
arms.note: a new --fix pass keeps the previous pass's project index, so the checks answer from sources the pass already rewrote

arms.name: M-NO-WIRE
arms.note: the one read that wires sameLine.comprehensionFor is gone, so the key goes back to the inert state S77 found it in

arms.name: M-PATHWALK-NULL
arms.note: a member path resolves to nothing, so comparison-to-boolean stops learning the type of a field-access operand. A fragment rather than a force: the member is inline, and a forced return ahead of the body is a non-final return the compiler refuses

arms.name: M-ROOTS-THIRDPARTY
arms.note: the declared resolutionRoots are tagged third-party along with the library, so a write from a project module outside the lint scope stops vetoing

arms.name: M-RTTI-FALSE
arms.note: no type carries @:rtti, so prefer-enum-abstract's rtti refusal never fires

arms.name: M-SEAM-BLIND
arms.note: no join can ever re-form S, so arm A claims the two-space squeeze is redundant and the autofix deletes a required loop again

arms.name: M-SHADOWEXT-TRUE
arms.note: every member reads as shadowing a `using` extension, so prefer-count takes the qualified `Lambda.count(xs, …)` spelling and inserts no `using`

arms.name: M-SUBOVERRIDE-TRUE
arms.note: every property reads as overridden below, so trivial-getter refuses every collapse it should make

arms.name: M-SUPERDECLARES-FALSE
arms.note: no supertype declares anything, so a backing-field owner binding stops being classified through its foreign supertype

arms.name: M-UNRELATED-FALSE
arms.note: no two classes are provably unrelated, so impossible-cast and impossible-is-check stop reporting

arms.name: M-WRITEINDEX-PROJECT-FINAL
arms.note: prefer-final-public-field goes back to a project-scoped write index, so a write through a third-party subtype is invisible again

arms.name: M-WRITEINDEX-PROJECT-READONLY
arms.note: prefer-read-only-field goes back to a project-scoped write index, so a write through a third-party subtype is invisible again

arms.name: M-EXPR-ELSE-KEEP
arms.note: `sameLine.expressionIf: next` maps the else-gap back to `Keep`, so a value-`if` with a `{ … }` branch reproduces whatever break the source wrote while its statement twin joins

arms.name: M-EXPR-ELSE-PLAIN-SAME
arms.note: the refuted cheap fix, wired as an arm: `next` maps onto a plain `Same`, so the shape-aware bracket arm joins an `else` onto a `]` and the curly `;` drop stops firing

arms.name: M-KEEP-JOINS
arms.note: `sameLine.expressionIf: keep` stops meaning keep for the else-gap and joins a break the config asked to preserve

arms.name: M-ELSE-BODY-SAME
arms.note: the else BODY stops following `expressionIf: next`, so the shape-aware forced break is suppressed and `SameOnBlock` joins an `else` onto an object-literal close

arms.name: M-ARM-PATH-FLAT
arms.note: a dotted type path stops becoming a directory path, so every arm resolves to a file that does not exist and the addressability gate can check nothing

arms.name: M-CURLY-CTORS-NONE
arms.note: no branch ctor reads as a CURLY block, so the shape-aware separator sends every value-`if` branch to the hardline arm and the `} else` join stops firing

arms.name: M-SBE-UNGATED
arms.find: final emit: Expr = dropTest == null ? policyDispatch : macro (_sbeSibling && $dropTest ? _de() : $policyDispatch);
arms.replace: final emit: Expr = dropTest == null ? policyDispatch : macro ($dropTest ? _de() : $policyDispatch);
arms.note: the optional `;` drop stops being gated on a following sibling, so an else-less value-`if` loses the terminator its enclosing statement needs

arms.name: M-TRAILOPT-KEEP-OFF
arms.note: no body field keeps its `@:trailOpt(';')` slot, so the `;` after an unterminated `#if` region body is dropped and the next statement fails with `Missing ;`

arms.name: M-TRAILOPT-KEEP-PRESENCE-BLIND
arms.note: the kept slot stops reading source presence, so a region whose branches carry their own `;` gains a second one after `#end`

arms.name: M-TRAILOPT-KEEP-UNGATED
arms.note: the slot is kept for every body, not just a `#if` region, so the redundant `;` after a de-braced block comes back as `;;`

arms.name: M-TRAILSEP-KEEP-OFF
arms.note: a block's trailing `;` after a `#if` region is dropped again like any `stmtNoSemi` tail, so `#end;` before `}` loses the only terminator of the region's last branch

arms.name: M-TRAILSEP-KEEP-ALL
arms.note: every source `;` after a block's last element is kept, so the redundant one after a closing `}` comes back

arms.name: M-SEP-GLUE-OFF
arms.note: an element's separator goes after its trailing comment again, so `#end; // c` comments out its own terminator and `fmt` refuses the file

arms.name: M-REGION-TERM-OFF
arms.note: no region owns the terminator after its `#end`, so a fix moving the region drops it and `empty-statement` deletes it

arms.name: M-INVERT-REGION-UNGUARDED
arms.note: a then-region closed only by the `else` is swapped into the tail slot with no terminator

arms.name: M-SKIPSCAN-SCOPEWIDE
arms.note: the skip-parse scan spans the whole resolution scope again, so a skip-parsing library source that merely SPELLS a project member name vetoes the candidate

arms.name: M-CHECKINDEX-PROJECT-FINAL
arms.find: final index: SymbolIndex = RefactorSupport.resolutionIndexOf(plugin) ?? SymbolIndex.build(scope, plugin);
arms.note: prefer-final-public-field goes back to a project-scoped name/type index, so a library supertype, interface or build macro is unresolvable again

arms.name: M-CHECKINDEX-PROJECT-READONLY
arms.find: final index: SymbolIndex = RefactorSupport.resolutionIndexOf(plugin) ?? SymbolIndex.build(scope, plugin);
arms.note: prefer-read-only-field goes back to a project-scoped name/type index, so a library supertype, interface or build macro is unresolvable again

arms.name: M-PLAINCLASS-SCOPEBLIND
arms.replace:
final named: Array<ResolvedType> = _index.refs.resolvedDeclsNamed(SourceText.lastSegment(path));
		final resolved: Null<ResolvedType> = named.length == 1 ? named[0] : null;
arms.note: the plain-class proof goes back to a scope-blind global uniqueness count, so a type the candidate file can neither import nor reach by package frees the candidate

arms.name: M-TRY-BODY-SYM-OFF
arms.note: the try BODY stops going through `SingleStmtBraces.trySymmetryBody`, so a bare body opposite a braced catch keeps its asymmetry instead of gaining a block of its own

arms.name: M-TRY-CATCHES-SYM-OFF
arms.note: the catch LIST stops going through `SingleStmtBraces.trySymmetryCatches`, so a braced group never de-braces and every catch but the last keeps the `;` Haxe rejects in front of `catch`

arms.name: M-NONCURLY-SAME-DROP
arms.note: a `[ … ]` block ctor separator falls back to the curly switch, where `SameOnBlock` matches no case and lands on the default space - so a bracket branch loses the source break the policy promised it

arms.name: M-NEWLINE-SIGNALS-NONE
arms.note: no downstream field contributes a captured-newline signal, so the conditional-expression seam has nothing to read and the source ladder collapses onto one line

arms.name: M-WORDOP-NO-RESTORE
arms.note: the operator loop stops rewinding to `_preWsPos` when the token that ended it is a WORD operator, so the trivia the loop consumed is lost and a conditional region after a metadata block no longer parses

arms.name: M-BLANK-MULTILINE-OFF
arms.find: if (optField == null) return { markExpr: macro {}, seenExpr: macro {}, applyExpr: macro {} };
arms.replace: if (true) return { markExpr: macro {}, seenExpr: macro {}, applyExpr: macro {} };
arms.note: the knob wires empty mark/seen/apply splices whatever the grammar asked for, so nothing measures a multiline member and no blank is inserted around one

arms.name: M-SSB-WRAP-DIRECTION
arms.find: final isThenBodyExpr: Expr = elseFieldName != null ? macro true : macro false;
arms.note: an `if` then-body stops identifying itself as one, so it is exempted from gate 8 alongside the loop bodies and a bare then opposite a braced else is never wrapped

arms.name: M-SSB-TRAIL-COMMENT-OFF
arms.note: the de-braced statement's same-line trailing comment is never hoisted, so it stays inside the block the unwrap just removed and leaves the output

arms.name: M-SSB-FRAME-OFF
arms.find:
final ssbSuppressCond: Null<Expr> = elseAccess == null
	? null
arms.note: the `_setSsbSuppress` frame is never armed, so an unwrap nested inside a then-body stops being gated on the trailing `else` and a dangling else loses the braces that keep it bound

arms.name: M-SSB-CHAIN-OFF
arms.find:
final thenChainSuppressExpr: Expr = elseAccess == null
	? macro false
arms.replace:
final thenChainSuppressExpr: Expr = true
	? macro false
arms.note: chain symmetry stops forcing braces, so one keeper branch of an else-if chain no longer makes its bare siblings keep theirs

arms.name: M-SSB-TAIL-SEALED-NONE
arms.note: no ctor reads as sealing its own tail, so a block, switch or do-while at the end of a body stops shielding the trailing `else` and the branch keeps braces it does not need

arms.name: M-SSB-OPEN-TRAIL-NONE
arms.note: a body whose single statement carries an OPEN trailing comment reads as carrying none, so the comment stops travelling with the statement the de-brace lifts out

arms.name: M-SSB-DANGLING-NONE
arms.note: no statement tail reads as a dangling `if`, so the de-brace stops refusing a body whose last statement would capture the enclosing `else`

arms.name: M-EICR-BOUNDARY-SKIP
arms.find: case WrapBoundary(inner): afterCond ? rewrap(scan(inner, trailing, true), d -> Doc.WrapBoundary(d)) : Scanning(true);
arms.note: a `WrapBoundary` past the condition is skipped whole instead of scanned, so the body's own boundary hides the anchor and every else-if comment reflow refuses

arms.name: M-EICR-HEADTEXT-ANY
arms.note: every rendered token reads as head text, so a `//`, a `}` or a `;` no longer ends the head line and the comment anchors past the position it belongs to

arms.name: M-EICR-SOFTLINE-ANCHOR
arms.note: a width-only break anchors the comment as readily as an unconditional one, so a body that merely COULD break takes the trailing comment the reflow was written to refuse

arms.name: M-EICR-KNOB-IGNORED
arms.note: the runtime gate stops reading `opt.elseIfCommentReflow`, so the reflow fires with the knob off and every pre-knob layout moves

arms.name: M-SSB-DOBODY-KEEP
arms.note: the do-body arm stops substituting its single clean statement for the block, so `do { g(); } while (c)` keeps braces the suppress frame is explicitly told not to gate

arms.name: M-LOOPIF-NEVER
arms.note: the loop-body probe never sees an `if` with an `else`, so `loopBodyIfElseNext` never breaks the body under the header and every glued shape stays glued

arms.name: M-LOOPIF-ALWAYS
arms.note: the same probe answers yes for every body, so a bare guard `if` and a non-`if` body break under the loop header alongside the shape the knob exists for

arms.name: M-LOOPIF-POLICY-BLIND
arms.find: final loopPolicy: Expr = loopIfElseTest == null ? optFlag : macro ($loopIfElseTest ? $nextPat : $optFlag);
arms.note: the loop-body `if`/`else` shape stops substituting `Next` for the placement, so `loopBodyIfElseNext` is inert at every `forBody` / `whileBody` / `doWhileBody` value and the reported site glues again

arms.name: M-LOOPIF-KEEP-BLIND
arms.find: return { expr: ESwitch(policyFlag, outerKeepCases, bodySwitch), pos: Context.currentPos() };
arms.replace: return { expr: ESwitch(optFlag, outerKeepCases, bodySwitch), pos: Context.currentPos() };
arms.note: the outer `Keep` switch reads the raw placement again, so a `keep` body routes to the source-preserving layout before any substitution can be seen - the S157 blind spot at `loopBodyIfElseNext`, and since S154 the bracket-hug substitution too, which is why `M-BRACKET-GLUE-KEEP-BLIND` cuts the same line one substitution narrower

arms.name: M-BRACKET-GLUE-KEEP-BLIND
arms.find: return { expr: ESwitch(policyFlag, outerKeepCases, bodySwitch), pos: Context.currentPos() };
arms.replace: return { expr: ESwitch(loopPolicy, outerKeepCases, bodySwitch), pos: Context.currentPos() };
arms.note: the outer `Keep` switch reads the placement from before the bracket substitution, so `expressionIfWithBrackets` goes blind at `sameLine.expressionIf: keep` and only there - the knob still cuddles `] else` through its two close seams and refuses the `[` hug, which is the half shape it exists to prevent

arms.name: M-LOOPIF-NOWRAP
arms.note: the one-level unwrap answers no, so a `do ... while` body - an `HxDoWhileBody.ExprBody` around the `if` - is invisible to the probe while the bare `for` / `while` body still reaches it

arms.name: M-SSB-TRY-SUBST-OFF
arms.note: the try/catch group verdict is computed and then not applied - neither the wrap direction nor the de-brace one reaches a body

arms.name: M-SSB-TRY-DEBRACE-NONE
arms.note: verdict 2 can no longer strip a braced try/catch body, so only the wrap direction of the group verdict survives

arms.name: M-SSB-BARE-ILLEGAL
arms.note: an ALREADY bare body blocks the group verdict instead of passing it, so a try/catch that is half de-braced is wrapped back up rather than finished

arms.name: M-SSB-VALUE-WRAP-OFF
arms.note: the value-if/value-try symmetry wrap never fires, so a bare branch opposite a braced one keeps its shape and the semicolon drop that rides on the wrap stops happening

arms.name: M-STRUCT-DECLARES-LOOSE
arms.note: structural conformance reads the absence walk's negation again, so an unresolvable supertype declares EVERY member and any subclass of an out-of-scope type conforms by member name

arms.name: M-STRUCT-NOMINAL-OPEN
arms.note: no written type is comparable, so the unification refutation never fires and a member SET match pins again whatever the two types are

arms.name: M-STRUCT-ALIAS-OPAQUE
arms.find:
final target: Null<String> = decl.type.aliasTargetRaw;
		return target == null || !_refs.markSeen(decl, seen) ? null : comparableNominalOf(target, decl, seen);
arms.note: a plain `typedef A = C` alias is compared as its own written name instead of being followed, so `{x:MyInt}` stops pinning a `var x:Int` the compiler does unify with it

arms.name: M-STRUCT-NULL-OPAQUE
arms.replace:
if (nominal == NULLABLE_WRAPPER_TYPE_NAME) return nominal;
		if (nominal == NULLABLE_WRAPPER_TYPE_NAME) {
arms.note: the nullability wrapper is compared as the nominal `Null`, so `{var x:Null<Int>}` stops pinning a `var x:Int` it accepts in both directions

arms.name: M-STRUCT-TYPEPARAM-CLOSED
arms.note: a structure member typed as its declaration's own type PARAMETER is compared as an ordinary nominal, so it refutes every argument it could have bound to

arms.name: M-STRUCT-DYNAMIC-CLOSED
arms.note: `Dynamic` is compared as an ordinary nominal, so a structure member declared `Dynamic` refutes every type it unifies with

arms.name: M-STRUCT-ANON-VAR-KEY
arms.note: the type maps are keyed on the member node again, so every anon-structure `var x:T;` / `final x:T;` field reads as unannotated and the conformance refutation cannot fire on one

arms.name: M-STRUCT-UNRESOLVED-OPEN
arms.note: a nominal that resolves nowhere is OPEN instead of compared by its written name, which is the sound reading for an out-of-scope alias and drops every refutation resting on an unresolved spelling

arms.name: M-STRUCT-ANON-CLOSED
arms.note: a nominal naming an ANONYMOUS-STRUCTURE typedef is compared as a name, so a structure member typed by one refutes every class that could unify with it

arms.name: M-NULLABLE-FLOW-REPORT-INDEX
arms.find: final index: SymbolIndex = RefactorSupport.resolutionIndexOf(plugin) ?? SymbolIndex.build(files, plugin);
arms.note: the flow seed asks the REPORT index again, so a nullable-returning member declared outside the reported files stops seeding anything

arms.name: M-NULLABLE-INDEX-EXCLUSION
arms.note: the exclusion key can never match, so `Array.pop` comes back through the index lookup the build-time filter never sees and the length-guarded accessors seed the flow again

arms.name: M-NULLABLE-REPORT-INDEX
arms.find: final index: SymbolIndex = RefactorSupport.resolutionIndexOf(plugin) ?? SymbolIndex.build(files, plugin);
arms.note: the cross-file return arc asks the REPORT index again, so every member declared outside the reported files is unknown and the arc is dead where it matters

arms.name: M-DECL-NULLABLE-OVERRIDES-EXISTS
arms.note: the written annotation is consulted even where the initializer already had a verdict, so a map read an `m.exists(k)` guard proved present is seeded MaybeNull again through its `Null<V>` declaration

arms.name: M-DECL-NULLABLE-BLIND
arms.note: the written `Null<T>` on a local declaration stops being evidence, so a receiver no nullable EXPRESSION feeds goes back to Unknown and the declaration-side half of the flow seed is dead

arms.name: M-NULLABLE-NO-CHAIN
arms.note: the receiver type is the written annotation or nothing, so every field-path / call receiver falls back to unknown and the null family stops seeing the sources only the chain resolver names

arms.name: M-NULLABLE-WRAPPER-OPAQUE
arms.note: the lossy `Null` that `declaredTypes` records for a `Null<Map<K, V>>` counts as an answer again, so a wrapped receiver goes back to being a safe miss

arms.name: M-SAFENAV-NO-NARROW
arms.note: a `?.` guard narrows nothing, so `if (u?.b != null) u.b.c()` reports its own guarded dereference again

arms.name: M-OPAQUE-REGION-BRACE-DELTA
arms.replace:

arms.name: M-HOIST-RETARGET-BAND
arms.note: a second declaration of the imported simple name is never a retarget, so the ambient statement silently replaces a same-package, root-package or wildcard-reached namesake in the modules that never spelled it

arms.name: M-HOIST-USING-DEMOTION
arms.note: a `using` is lifted out of a module that keeps another one, so the extension it held loses its position to the rival that stays and every method both modules declare resolves elsewhere

arms.name: M-HOIST-CHAIN-INHERITED
arms.note: a statement the chain above a directory already puts in force is proposed again, so a nested ambient source repeats its own parent

arms.name: M-HOIST-GUARDED-BLIND
arms.find: if (imp.guarded || SymbolIndex.bindsAnyOf(imp, statement.names, ctx.publicTypes)) return false;
arms.note: a chain carrying a `#if`-guarded statement is added to anyway, so a position this rule writes joins a chain whose every resolution answers the union of two build configurations

arms.name: M-HOIST-SHORT-CHAIN
arms.note: a governed module whose chain is knowingly SHORT is judged anyway, so the statement is added against bindings the engine never saw

arms.name: M-HOIST-MIN-MODULES
arms.note: a directory with too few modules for a share to mean anything is weighed anyway, so one module of two carries the whole verdict

arms.name: M-HOIST-SITE-ORDER
arms.note: the narrowest position is weighed first, so a statement lands in a nested source AND in its parent and the nested copy repeats what the parent already puts in force

arms.name: M-AMBIENT-CHAIN-STALE
arms.note: the memo of a directory chain and of the import maps keyed by path survives a pass that rewrote an ambient source, so every later pass of one --fix run resolves against the tree that was while the plugin behind the decorator reads disk fresh

arms.name: M-IMPORT-LEAF-ONLY-NAMES
arms.note: an import statement is read as binding its LEAF name alone, so a statement naming a module stops carrying the siblings that module declares and both import rules decide a name they never look at

arms.name: M-ORACLE-FIRST-CONFIGURATION-IS-ENOUGH
arms.find: final asked: Array<OracleConfig> = cut < 0 ? oracles : oracles.slice(0, cut + 1);
arms.note: only the FIRST configuration is ever asked, so an edit that compiles under one set of defines and breaks another is applied - the cross-configuration hole the list exists to close

arms.name: M-ORACLE-RED-BASELINE-STOPS-THE-PHASE
arms.note: any configuration red before the run stops the whole phase again, so one broken target leaves every risky fix report-only - including in files that target never reads and a green configuration verifies

arms.name: M-ORACLE-COVERAGE-PAIRED-BY-INDEX
arms.replace: return [for (i in 0...oracles.length) i < memo.probes.length ? memo.probes[i].coverage : probedFor(memo, oracles[i])];
arms.note: a seeded probe is handed to whichever configuration sits at its position, so a phase judging a different subset reads another build's compiled set and verifies an edit the judging build never compiles

arms.name: M-ORACLE-UNKNOWN-COVERAGE-STOPS-THE-PHASE
arms.note: one configuration whose compiled set is unknown stops the whole phase again, so its known siblings judge nothing - the policy a red baseline no longer follows

arms.name: M-ORACLE-EXCLUSIONS-UNNAMED
arms.note: the driver stops naming excluded configurations, so a net or phase shrunk to the green subset reads as covering every build

arms.name: M-DISPLAY-ORACLE-DROPS-DEFINES
arms.note: the display server is warmed and queried without its configuration's defines, so it names types for a build nobody judges

arms.name: M-ORACLE-UNKNOWN-COVERAGE-NO-VETO
arms.note: a configuration whose compiled set is unknown is dropped from the post-edit typecheck, so an edit that compiles on the covering build and breaks the unknown one is applied although its green baseline makes the rejection attributable

arms.name: M-ORACLE-EXCLUSIONS-KEYED-BY-SENTENCE
arms.note: exclusions are deduped by sentence, so a red build whose error line moved after a safe fix is named twice with two reasons

arms.name: M-GENERATE-NEVER-STALE-BY-INPUT
arms.find: for (input in inputs) if (hashIn(recordedInputs, input) != hashOf(input, memo)) return '$input changed';
arms.note: a changed generateInputs file no longer makes the recorded generation stale, so an hxml generated from an older project.xml keeps answering for a build that no longer exists

arms.name: M-GENERATE-NEVER-STALE-BY-COMMAND
arms.find: if (record.command != group.generate.command) return 'its generate command changed';
arms.note: a changed generate command no longer regenerates, so an entry whose recipe was edited keeps the hxml the old recipe wrote

arms.name: M-GENERATE-TRUSTS-A-MISSING-HXML
find: for (hxml in group.hxmls) if (!sys.FileSystem.exists(hxml)) return '$hxml is missing';
for (hxml in group.hxmls) if (hashIn(recordedOutputs, hxml) != hashOf(hxml, memo)) return '$hxml changed since it was generated';
arms.note: an hxml deleted or edited after its generation was recorded is read as current, so the configuration compiles a missing or hand-edited file

arms.name: M-GENERATE-FAILURE-USES-THE-STALE-HXML
arms.note: a failed generate command no longer makes its configuration unavailable, so the hxml an earlier generation left behind silently answers for the build

arms.name: M-SPAWN-RUN-IGNORES-CWD
arms.note: a single haxe spawn runs in the process cwd whatever the configuration's dir says, so a relative -cp resolves against the wrong tree and the typecheck and every probe answer about a different project

arms.name: M-SPAWN-RUNALL-IGNORES-CWD
arms.find: const opts = { cwd: j.cwd == null ? undefined : j.cwd,
arms.note: the parallel driver spawns every job in its own cwd rather than the job's, so overlapped typechecks and coverage probes of a configuration with a dir answer about a different tree

arms.name: M-DRIVER-CANCELS-EARLIER-JOBS
arms.find: for (let k = i + 1; k < jobs.length; k++)
arms.note: a failing job also kills the jobs declared BEFORE it, so the overlapped verdict is the first failure to finish rather than the first in declared order

arms.name: M-ORACLE-CACHE-IGNORES-DIR
arms.note: the verdict fingerprint resolves the hxml's classpath against the process cwd, so an edit under the configuration's dir leaves a stored verdict matching

arms.name: M-DISPLAY-IGNORES-DIR
arms.note: the display server is warmed and queried from the process cwd, so a configuration with a dir never warms and the oracle-assisted phase is skipped

arms.name: M-GENERATE-HASHES-INPUTS-AFTER-THE-RUN
arms.note: the explicit inputs are hashed after the command instead of before, so an edit landing during a generation is recorded beside an hxml built from the old content and never regenerates

arms.name: M-GENERATE-RECORD-OUTLIVES-THE-RUN
arms.note: the previous generation's record survives while a stale command runs, so a generation killed half way leaves a partial tree that reads as current forever

arms.name: M-GENERATE-DIRECTORY-INPUT-CONSTANT
arms.note: a directory input hashes to one constant, so a file added or edited under it never regenerates

arms.name: M-GENERATE-FIRST-ENTRY-INPUTS
arms.find: held.inputs = mine == null || theirs == null ? null : theirs.concat([for (input in mine) if (!theirs.contains(input)) input]);
arms.note: entries sharing one command keep only the first entry's inputs, so a change to an input only a later entry declares never regenerates

arms.name: M-GENERATE-LOCK-IGNORED
arms.note: every lock holder reads as dead, so a live run's exclusive hold is taken over and its tree regenerated under it

arms.name: M-GENERATE-LOCK-NEVER-RECOVERED
arms.note: a lock left by a dead run is waited for as if its owner lived, so one crashed run makes every later one unavailable

arms.name: M-GENERATE-EMPTY-INPUTS-NEVER
arms.note: an empty generateInputs list is kept, so the entry never regenerates while an absent list regenerates every run

arms.name: M-GENERATE-MISSING-INPUT-SILENT
arms.find: drops.push('compilerOracle[$index] "generateInputs" names $input, which does not exist — kept, it counts once created');
arms.note: a generateInputs path that does not exist is accepted silently, so a typo makes that input a constant nobody hears about

arms.name: M-DRIVER-NEVER-STOPS
arms.note: a failing job no longer ends the later ones, so a rejection waits for and pays every compile declared after it

arms.name: M-DRIVER-KILLS-ONLY-THE-SHELL
arms.note: a kill reaches only the shell, so a build tool it started keeps writing into the generated tree after its job was cancelled

arms.name: M-DRIVER-NO-TIMEOUT
arms.find: if (j.timeout > 0) c.timer = setTimeout(() => { c.timedOut = true; kill(c); }, j.timeout);
arms.note: a job's timeout is ignored, so a hung generate command blocks the run forever

arms.name: M-ORACLE-CACHE-STORES-A-MOVED-FINGERPRINT
arms.find: if (OracleCache.fingerprint(hxml, cwd, defines, memo) != fingerprint) return false;
arms.note: a verdict is filed under the pre-compile fingerprint even when the tree moved during the compile, so a verdict about a half-regenerated tree is handed to the next run of the complete one

arms.name: M-GENERATE-IGNORES-LIBRARY-STATE
arms.note: the library state the generated hxml names is not an input, so a haxelib version or dev-path switch leaves an hxml naming the old library paths current

arms.name: M-GENERATE-READERS-EXCLUDE-EACH-OTHER
arms.note: every run takes every generation exclusively, so one agent's long --fix run blocks every other lint over a tree nobody regenerates

arms.name: M-GENERATE-WRITER-IGNORES-READERS
arms.note: a regeneration no longer waits for the runs still compiling the old tree, so its rm -rf lands under their typecheck

arms.name: M-GENERATE-OWNERLESS-ABANDONED-AT-ONCE
arms.note: a writer caught between its mkdir and its owner write is taken over at once, so two runs both hold the lock

arms.name: M-GENERATE-TAKEOVER-UNVERIFIED
arms.find: final same: Bool = current != null && current.identity == stale.identity;
arms.note: a run that judged an owner dead too late removes the fresh writer that replaced it, so two runs both win the takeover

arms.name: M-GENERATE-PID-ALONE
arms.note: a lock owner is judged by its pid alone, so a pid the system reused keeps a dead run's lock for hours

arms.name: M-DRIVER-SIGNAL-ORPHANS
arms.find: for (const s of ['SIGINT', 'SIGTERM', 'SIGHUP']) process.on(s, () => { killAll(); drop(); process.exit(1); });
arms.note: a signalled driver exits without its detached job groups, so Ctrl-C leaves a build tool writing into dist/oracle

arms.name: M-GENERATE-REPO-DIR-FROM-NAME
arms.note: a dev install is not traced to the repository directory whose .dev points at it, so haxelib dev on a library whose json name differs from its directory never regenerates

arms.name: M-GENERATE-IMPLICIT-HASHED-AFTER-THE-RUN
arms.note: implicit inputs are hashed only after the command, so a library switched while it ran is recorded as the state the hxml was built against

arms.name: M-GENERATE-HASH-MEMO-UNUSED
arms.note: every generation naming a path reads and hashes it again, so a large shared input such as fonts/ is read once per build per run

arms.name: M-GENERATE-TEMPLATES-UNTRACKED
arms.note: a library's code templates are not inputs, so a changed lime ApplicationMain template leaves the generated sources stale

arms.name: M-ORACLE-CACHE-MEMO-UNREAD
arms.note: the fingerprint memo is never read, so every configuration re-reads and re-hashes the whole source tree before and after the compiles

arms.name: M-GENERATE-PRODUCED-INCLUDE-IS-INPUT
arms.note: an hxml the generation writes and includes is compared across the run as if it were an input, so every generation that rewrites it goes unrecorded and regenerates forever (lime's iOS Build.hxml)

arms.name: M-GENERATE-SHARED-HELD-INTO-PHASE-TWO
arms.note: a run keeps its shared holds while it waits for exclusive ones, so two runs that each find two generations stale wait for each other until the deadline and each loses a configuration

arms.name: M-GENERATE-CLAIM-NEVER-CLEARED
arms.note: a takeover claim left by a run that died mid-takeover is never cleared, so every later run waits on a writer nobody can take over

arms.name: M-GENERATE-TAKEOVER-LEAVES-THE-JOB
arms.note: a takeover removes the dead run's writer while its generate job still runs, so that build tool writes on into a tree the next generation owns

arms.name: M-GENERATE-FORMAT-UNCHECKED
arms.find: if (record.format != FORMAT_TAG) return 'its generation was recorded by an older engine';
arms.note: a record written under an older scheme is trusted, so records whose implicit inputs an older engine derived differently keep answering as current

arms.name: M-GENERATE-PRODUCED-BY-ROOT
arms.note: any include under a wider tree than the hxml's own output directory counts as produced, so an edited project hxml the generated one includes goes unnoticed during a generation

arms.name: M-DRIVER-OUTLIVES-ITS-PARENT
arms.find: setInterval(() => { if (process.ppid !== parent) { killAll(); drop(); process.exit(1); } }, 500).unref();
arms.note: a driver whose apq was SIGKILLed keeps its jobs running, so the next run regenerates concurrently with an orphaned build tool

arms.name: M-GENERATE-SHARE-WITHOUT-REJUDGE
arms.note: a group judged current before another run wiped it is shared for the compile without being judged again, so a half-written tree is typechecked and vetoes an edit falsely

arms.name: M-GENERATE-REJUDGE-UNBOUNDED
arms.find: refuse(run, group, 'it went stale again $attempts time(s) while this run waited — another run keeps moving it');
arms.note: a group still stale after the bounded retries is handed to the compile anyway instead of being made unavailable

arms.name: M-GENERATE-STATE-IN-TMPDIR
arms.note: the generation record and lock live under TMPDIR, so runs with different TMPDIRs share no lock and rm -rf the same tree concurrently

arms.name: M-GENERATE-STATE-DIR-HASHED
arms.note: a directory input that holds the generation root hashes hxq's own state, which every generation rewrites, so it never reads as current

arms.name: M-GENERATE-STATE-NOT-IGNORED
arms.note: the state directory's .gitignore matches nothing, so every project has to list .apq/ in its own ignore file again

arms.name: M-GENERATE-IGNORE-OVERWRITTEN
arms.note: an ignore file already inside the state directory is rewritten on every run, discarding whatever the project put there

arms.name: M-GENERATE-ORDER-BY-KEY
arms.note: waits follow the declaration key rather than the lock identity, so two runs declaring one tree under different commands can take its locks in opposite orders

arms.name: M-GENERATE-ENDJOB-PID-ONLY
arms.note: a left job with no recorded start time is killed on its pid alone, which may name an unrelated process group by now

arms.name: M-GENERATE-SHARE-JUDGES-STALENESS
arms.note: the compile hold asks whether a group is current instead of whether it moved since this run looked, so an entry with no inputs, or one whose command writes its own input, is regenerated until it is given up on

arms.name: M-GENERATE-RIVAL-COMMAND-RETRIED
arms.note: a tree another configuration regenerated with a different command is sent back through regeneration, so two configurations take it back and forth instead of one being told why it is unavailable

arms.name: M-GENERATE-RIVAL-COMMANDS-KEPT
arms.note: an hxml two different generate commands of one config claim is kept, so both commands run into one tree and one configuration is always unavailable

arms.name: M-GENERATE-READ-ONLY-ROOT-THROWS
arms.find: return 'cannot create its generation state under ${Path.directory(Path.directory(stateDir(group)))}: ${exception.message}';
arms.note: a generation root where the state cannot be created crashes the run instead of making its configurations unavailable

arms.name: M-GENERATE-STATE-BY-CONFIG-ROOT
arms.note: the generation state lives beside the declaring config, so two configs over one tree take two locks and delete the tree under each other

arms.name: M-GENERATE-STATE-BY-SPELLING
arms.note: the generation state is keyed by the hxml as spelled, so a symlinked spelling of one tree takes a second lock

arms.name: M-GENERATE-STATE-IN-OUTPUT-DIR
arms.note: a project marker in the hxml's own directory puts the generation state inside the tree the command may delete

arms.name: M-GENERATE-STATE-ROOT-FROM-HXML
arms.note: the project root is searched from above the hxml, so a marker the generation writes at its output root holds the state it deletes, and a top-level hxml climbs into an enclosing repository

arms.name: M-GENERATE-RIVAL-BY-SPELLING
arms.note: two spellings of one hxml under two commands are not seen as rivals, so both commands run into one tree

arms.name: M-GENERATE-EPOCH-UNOBSERVED
arms.note: another run's generation that left the record and hxml as they were goes unseen, though it rewrote the rest of the tree

arms.name: M-GENERATE-RACED-VERIFIES-FIXES
arms.note: a generation that raced an input still verifies --fix, so a build that does not match the tree can veto a sound fix

arms.name: M-ORACLE-SUMMARY-SILENT
arms.note: apq oracle ends without counting the unavailable configurations, so its exit 0 reads as every configuration confirmed

arms.name: M-FIAD-CROSS-SUPER-UNPROVED
arms.note: the crossing narrowings never hold, so every init hoisted across an explicit `super(...)` is refused again - the blanket refusal that made the rule silent on openfl display classes

arms.name: M-FIAD-EARLY-READ-IGNORED
arms.note: no occurrence of the field ever counts as observable, so an early read that compares, defaults, stores or passes on the `null` no longer refuses the crossing move

arms.name: M-FIAD-EARLY-READ-CALL-ARG
arms.replace: return parent != null && (index == 0 || parent.kind == scan.shape.callKind) && scan.faultingKinds.contains(parent.kind);
arms.note: a call ARGUMENT is admitted as a null-faulting position, so a crossing init whose field is passed on as a value moves and the callee now sees `[]` where it saw `null`

arms.name: M-FIAD-EARLY-READ-SAME-FILE
arms.note: the early-read scan looks at the field's own file only, so a subclass in another file reading the early `null` in a value position no longer refuses the move

arms.name: M-FIAD-INERT-ADMITS-ALL
arms.note: every right-hand side reads as an inert collection, so a `new`, a static call, a literal holding an identifier, a bare string or a bare scalar is hoisted ahead of the base constructor

arms.name: M-FIAD-CROSS-SUPER-NO-SOLE
arms.note: the crossing path no longer demands the sole write, so a field another member also writes moves across `super(...)` and a write the base constructor reaches outlives the deleted init

arms.name: M-FIAD-CROSS-SUPER-CHAIN
arms.note: the fix-side chain reading admits a crossing init as a co-mover, so a refused crossing init holds back the fix of an accepted one after it

arms.name: M-FIAD-DENOTES-ALL
arms.note: every occurrence of the name is read as the field, so a same-named member of an unrelated type - a bare read or a `this.` one - blocks the move

arms.name: M-FIAD-INERT-ELEMENT-ADMITS-ALL
arms.note: every collection element reads as inert, so a literal holding a foreign static read or a call is evaluated ahead of the base constructor

arms.name: M-FIAD-CROSSING-ADMITS-SCALARS
arms.find: return collectionKinds.contains(node.kind) && node.children.foreach(c -> inertElement(c, plugin, shape));
arms.replace: return collectionKinds.contains(node.kind) ? node.children.foreach(c -> inertElement(c, plugin, shape)) : ConstantFieldScan.isConstantScalarInitializer(node, plugin) || (shape.stringLiteralKinds ?? []).contains(node.kind);
arms.note: a bare scalar or string crosses `super(...)` again, although a `null` String answers `length` on hxcpp instead of faulting

arms.name: M-FIAD-TRY-IGNORED
arms.note: a faulting read inside a `try` body counts as unobservable, although the catch turns the early `null` into working code that changes once the field is initialised

arms.name: M-FIAD-NO-ROOTS-ADMITTED
arms.note: a run whose project declared no `resolutionRoots` (a `resolutionLibs`-only scope) scans the report files alone, so a narrow `--fix` moves an init a reader in an unlinted file observes

arms.name: M-FIAD-ANY-DECLARED-TYPE
arms.note: every declared type is admitted, so an abstract whose `@:from` runs code (or whose method accepts a `null` receiver) takes a hoisted literal

arms.name: M-FIAD-PUBLIC-ADMITTED
arms.note: a public field (or one of a `@:publicFields` type) crosses `super(...)`, although code outside the project scope may read it early

arms.name: M-FIAD-TRY-BOUNDARY-CLEARED
arms.find: final childInTry: Bool = inTry || tryNode && child.kind != scan.catchKind;
arms.replace: final childInTry: Bool = !(scan.shape.functionKinds ?? []).concat(scan.shape.lambdaKinds ?? []).contains(node.kind) && (inTry || tryNode && child.kind != scan.catchKind);
arms.note: the try flag is cleared again at every function and lambda boundary, so a lambda or local function written inside a `try` and called there reads the early `null` under a catch that turns it into working code

arms.name: M-FIAD-SHADOW-IGNORED
arms.note: a core type name the file shadows - an imported, wildcard-reached or same-package user `Map` / `Array` - passes as the core type, so an abstract whose `@:from` runs code takes a hoisted literal

arms.name: M-FIAD-ROOTS-MATCH-IGNORED
arms.note: a declared `resolutionRoots` entry matching no `.hx` counts as a working root, so the crossing path admits an init over a scope that is the report alone

arms.name: M-FIAD-PROVEN-NEVER
arms.note: no crossing is ever proven, so an init after `super(...)` whose move nothing can observe is refused again whenever its right-hand side is no inert collection

arms.name: M-FIAD-PROVEN-ALWAYS
arms.note: every crossing counts as proven, with or without the truth: an init an override, a listener or a shared static can observe is hoisted ahead of the base constructor

arms.name: M-FIAD-PROVEN-NO-READER
arms.find: if (truth.mayReach(Region(file, crossed), field, Read) != Proven) return false;
arms.replace: if (false && truth.mayReach(Region(file, crossed), field, Read) != Proven) return false;
arms.note: the crossed code is never asked whether it can read the field, so a base constructor calling an override that reads it, or a listener the prefix fires, sees the value instead of nothing

arms.name: M-FIAD-PROVEN-NO-COMMUTE
arms.find: if (truth.mayReach(Region(file, crossed), { owner: r.owner, name: r.name }, changes) != Proven) return false;
arms.note: what the right-hand side reads is never checked against what the crossed code writes, so a construction reading a static the prefix sets runs before the prefix sets it

arms.name: M-FIAD-PROVEN-EXPOSED
arms.find: host.reachBuilds() == null || fieldExposed(tree, member, container, plugin, shape)
arms.note: a public field crosses too, though code outside the project may read it before the base constructor returns

arms.name: M-FRESH-ONLY-WRITES-ADMITTED
arms.note: a write of shared state the right-hand side's code makes is admitted, so a construction setting a static the base constructor reads moves ahead of the read

arms.name: M-FRESH-ONLY-STATEFUL-LIBRARY
arms.note: a pure library call that advances hidden state (`Math.random`) is skipped as harmless, so two draws the move reorders are taken to commute

arms.name: M-FRESH-ONLY-ENTRY-FACETED
arms.find: if (!view.faceted(g, file, span)) return Unconfined(file, span, 'the compiler facts do not describe the code');
arms.note: a right-hand side in a file the run rewrote reads as reading nothing, so the next `--fix` pass hoists an init whose static read the base constructor changes

arms.name: M-ISVAR-SLOTS-ANY
arms.note: every accessor slot counts as storageless, so an @:isVar over a `default` / `null` slot that has storage anyway is reported

arms.name: M-ISVAR-INIT-BLIND
arms.note: a declaration initializer is ignored, so the fix strips the metadata an `= v` needs to write the field

arms.name: M-ISVAR-ACCESSOR-BODY-BLIND
arms.note: accessor bodies are never read, so the fix strips the metadata from a property whose get_x / set_x, or a subclass override of one, reads or writes the field

arms.name: M-ISVAR-BYPASS-BLIND
arms.note: an @:bypassAccessor construct is never read, so the fix strips the metadata from a field a bypass access still reaches

arms.name: M-ISVAR-SCOPE-REPORT-ONLY
arms.note: the storage scan reads the report set alone, so a one-file lint misses an override in a resolution-scope subclass that writes the field

arms.name: M-ISVAR-REFLECTION-BLIND
arms.note: a reflective string naming the property is ignored, so the fix removes a field `Reflect.field` reads by name

arms.name: M-ISVAR-RTTI-BLIND
arms.note: an @:rtti owner is judged like any other, so the fix changes the field set its runtime type information describes

arms.name: M-ISVAR-CHAIN-UNRESOLVED-ADMITTED
arms.note: an owner whose supertype chain does not resolve is judged anyway, so an ancestor the index never read may carry what reaches the field

arms.name: M-ISVAR-OPAQUE-BLIND
arms.find: if (CondRegionScan.opaqueCondRegionMentioning(tree, entry.source, name, ctx.shape) != null) return true;
arms.note: an unparsed `#if` region spelling the name is trusted as empty, although nothing inside it projects for the scan to see

arms.name: M-ISVAR-MACRO-FIXED
arms.note: a finding on a macro-built owner is fixed without a compiler oracle, so the metadata a builder's generated access may need is removed unverified

arms.name: M-ISVAR-MACRO-NEVER-ADMITTED
arms.note: a macro-built owner's finding is declined even under a compiler oracle, so the verified path the oracle offers never removes its metadata

arms.name: M-ISVAR-NATIVE-BLIND
arms.note: target code pasted as a string is not read, so the fix strips the metadata a `__cpp__` / `Syntax.code` / `@:functionCode` access needs, and only the native build fails

arms.name: M-ISVAR-MEMBER-KEEP-BLIND
arms.find: if (retained != null && run.exists(n -> MemberKinds.META_KINDS.contains(n.kind) && n.name == retained)) return null;
arms.note: a member-level `@:keep` is ignored, so a member pinned against removal by machinery no scan models loses its storage

arms.name: M-ISVAR-EMPTY-CALL-UNFIXED
arms.note: an argument-less `@:isVar()` is reported but `fix` answers no edit and no reason for it

arms.name: M-ULB-VALUE-ITERATION-NEVER
arms.note: no iterable is proved to iterate the same values, so an unread key over an Array or List is spelled `_` instead of dropped

arms.name: M-ULB-VALUE-ITERATION-ALWAYS
arms.note: every iterable counts as proved, so an unread key over a Map is dropped although its keyValueIterator reads a removed entry back as null

arms.name: M-ULB-VALUE-ITERATION-SHADOW-BLIND
arms.find: if (stdPath == null || shadowedByNonStdType(index, nominal)) return null;
arms.note: a project type named List is taken for the std one, so its key is dropped against an iterator() it may not have

arms.name: M-ULB-WILDCARD-KEY-ADMITTED
arms.note: a key already spelled `_` is judged like any other, so `for (_ in xs)` is reported as unread and a discarded key is taken from redundant-map-iter-key

arms.name: M-ULB-OUTER-WILDCARD-BLIND
arms.note: a body read of an outer `_` is ignored, so the renamed binder captures it

arms.name: M-ULB-SHADOW-COUNTED-AS-READ
arms.note: a read of an inner shadow is left unaccounted, so a binder the body only shadows is kept as though read

arms.name: M-ULB-OUTER-BINDING-AS-SHADOW
arms.note: a read resolving to the loop binder itself counts as a shadow, so a binder read before its re-declaration is renamed

arms.name: M-ULB-INTERP-BLIND
arms.note: occurrences are never accounted for, so a `$i` interpolation read and anything else the tree hides is renamed away

arms.name: M-ULB-INTERP-LITERAL-BLIND
arms.note: an occurrence inside an interpolating literal is trusted once resolved, so a `${i}` read of a shadow no longer refuses

arms.name: M-ULB-COVERAGE-BLIND
arms.note: an occurrence no hit accounts for is trusted, so a read inside a macro reification is renamed away

arms.name: M-ULB-OPAQUE-COND-BLIND
