arms.name: M-TOUCH-ADOPTED-UNREAD
arms.note: a method a build macro made whose facts do not say how it names the member touches nothing, though no text holds it to read instead

arms.name: M-REACH-ENTRY-REWRITTEN
arms.find: if (facts == null || !facts.truth || tree == null) return null;
arms.replace: if (facts == null || tree == null || true) return null;
arms.note: an entry in code a build macro replaced is read as its text, which is none of what runs

arms.name: M-REACH-ENTRY-MEMBER
arms.note: a member question's region in code a build macro replaced is read as its text, which is none of what runs

arms.name: M-REACH-ENTRY-LOCAL
arms.note: a local question in code a build macro replaced is read as its text, which is none of what runs

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-ESCAPE-TYPED
arms.note: an escaping value is typed by the declarations alone, so one only the compiler types makes every instance escape

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-TOUCH-TYPED
arms.find: final typed: Null<String> = at == null ? null : g.facts?.view.typeSourceAt(g, file, at);
arms.note: a receiver the declarations do not type may be anything again, although the compiler typed it

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-MACRO
arms.find: truth && g != null && faceted(g, file, n.at.span) ? null : Reification(file, span);
arms.note: a macro's expansion is no blind spot, so the code it adds is never accounted for

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-DROPPED
arms.note: a table missing a configuration is read as if it held every build

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-REFLECT-VALUE
arms.find: for (r in n.reflection) if (r.isValue && meets(r.at.span, span)) return DynamicName(file, r.at.span);
arms.note: a reflective member read as a value is no blind spot, so the member it later reaches by name is never accounted for

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-BUILDS
arms.note: a build macro only the compiler saw applied never makes a type Unknown

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-GENERIC
arms.note: a @:generic instance is named by its own generated type, which no declaration holds, instead of its generic class

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-NATIVE-IDENT
arms.note: a call of a native identifier records nothing, so what it may run is never admitted

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-CONSTRUCTION
arms.note: a construction the facts record never runs the initializers of a generated constructor

arms.name: M-GRAPH-LOCAL-INLINE
arms.note: a local inline function is no node of the graph, so a call of it resolves to nothing and what it runs is never walked

arms.name: M-FACTS-CALL-SITE-INLINE
arms.note: only an `inline` method is matched to a splice, so a method its call site inlines reads as a macro expansion

arms.name: M-FACTS-SPLICE-OWN-ARGUMENTS
arms.note: a spliced body's own call-site arguments are searched for the method it came from, so a macro expansion is read as an inlined call of the caller itself

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-BIND
arms.note: a closure the compiler made is dropped, so the method a bound call runs is never used as a value

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-ALIKE
arms.find: var answer: Bool = typeAlike(owner) && declaredAlike(owner, name, true);
arms.note: a member whose declaration some build types differently is trusted as the listed builds typed it

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-GUARDED-NAME
arms.find: for (name in statics) if (guarded.exists(name)) return false;
arms.note: a call naming a member some build declares conditionally is trusted, though that build resolves it to the member

arms.name: M-FACTS-ABSTRACT-THIS
arms.find: final straddles: Bool = !inside && info.file == _home && info.min <= _max && info.max >= _min;
arms.note: a range meeting the body without lying inside it — an abstract method's own `this`, placed at the whole abstract — reads as a splice, and the method is marked as a macro expansion

arms.name: M-FACTS-ELEMENT-WRITE
arms.note: an element write leaves no fact, so an array written through its elements reads as never mutated

arms.name: M-FACTS-USE
arms.note: every field read is used as a value, so no read says it only calls, indexes or compares

arms.name: M-FACTS-HELD
arms.note: a field read held in a local is no longer followed through the local's reads, so a lowered loop's array reads as escaping

arms.name: M-FACTS-CAPTURE
arms.note: a local read from a nested function keeps its own use, so a captured field value reads as used in place

arms.name: M-FACTS-FRESH
arms.note: no field write is fresh, so a member only ever reset to a new array reads as holding a shared one

arms.name: M-FACTS-FRESH-DISCARDED
arms.note: a fresh value stored by an assignment used as a value counts as the field's alone, though the assignment hands it on

arms.name: M-FACTS-INLINED-RECEIVER
arms.find: final called: Null<String> = receiverCall(v, e.pos, block);
arms.note: the receiver of an inlined method is held in the compiler's local like any value, so the key-value loop's array reads as handed to `new ArrayKeyValueIterator` and escapes

arms.name: M-FACTS-RECEIVER-BLOCK
arms.find: if (at.file != around.file || at.min != around.min || at.max != around.max) return null;
arms.note: a local the inlined method's own code names `_this` counts as the compiler's receiver binding, so an argument it keeps reads as the receiver of a call of the array's own method

arms.name: M-FACTS-RECEIVER-PARAM
arms.note: a parameter named `_this`, bound by the compiler as it binds a receiver, counts as the receiver, so the argument it keeps reads as the receiver of a call of the array's own method

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-NESTED-OWNER
arms.find: if (owner != null && owner.id != node.id && owner.span.from == n.at.span.from) return null;
arms.note: a function with no typed body of its own is read through the facts of a function nested in it, which leave out what it runs itself

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-SYNTAX-UNION
arms.replace:
if (kind != Contains && facts?.muted.exists(from) == true) return;
indexEdge(edge);
arms.note: a faceted function records the facts' edges alone, so a name another build resolves the way the syntax reads it is lost

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-GUARDED-IMPORT
arms.find: if (guarded || conditional(text.file, text.source, header)) answer = false;
arms.note: a type in a file importing under a condition is trusted as the listed builds typed its members

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-LIBRARY-DYNAMIC
arms.note: a call of a library dynamic method the graph has not read records no edge, so its body is never read

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-UNREAD-VALUE
arms.note: the value channel is taken to run only code the walk enters, so a stored function's conversion is never admitted

arms.name: M-REACH-ABSTRACT-TEXT-ANY
arms.note: an abstract's own toString is taken to run on the abstract alone, though it may convert the value it wraps

arms.name: M-GRAPH-USING-META
arms.find: final bringing: Null<String> = types.firstOnChain(recv.typeName, t -> types.meta.bringsExtensions(t));
arms.note: a call no member declares resolves to the extensions the file's `using`s name, though a `@:using` on the receiver's type may supply another

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-USING-META
arms.note: a function naming a type that brings extensions in is read through the facts, which name the extension the listed builds resolved

arms.name: M-INDEX-GUARDED-META-LIFT
arms.find: final held: Array<QueryNode> = node.name == null ? [for (c in node.children) if (isMetaNodeKind(c.kind)) c] : [];
arms.note: metadata a conditional region holds alone is lifted nameless, so the declaration it annotates carries none of it

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-UNREAD-IMPLICIT
arms.note: code the walk never enters, read by its syntax, is taken to run no operator, index or literal member, only conversions and iterations

arms.name: M-FACTS-SOLE-MEMBER-NONE
arms.note: a member of a simple name several typed types share is never read by its id, so a library member only one of them declares keeps its syntax (openfl's `Vector.splice` beside `haxe.ds.Vector`)

arms.name: M-FACTS-SOLE-MEMBER-DECLARED
arms.note: a declaration of the member no build typed, which may run under another name, leaves the name one type's member

arms.name: M-ADMIT-SYNTAX-READ-UNTRUE
arms.note: facts that are not the truth narrow what code the walk never enters runs implicitly

arms.name: M-ADMIT-SYNTAX-READ-FACETED
arms.note: a function value read by its syntax is taken to run implicitly only what code read through its facts does

arms.name: M-ADMIT-SYNTAX-READ-UNSEEN
arms.note: library code the walk has not read is taken to run implicitly only what code read through its facts does

arms.name: M-ADMIT-SYNTAX-READ-FIELD
arms.note: (precision) a project field holding a function value counts as library code not read, so the facts never narrow a stored function's call

arms.name: M-REACH-UNREAD-NARROWED
arms.note: (precision) code read through facts that are the truth is taken to run any implicitly-called member, as code read by its syntax may

arms.name: M-REACH-UNREAD-RECHECK
arms.note: a narrowed unread admission is never widened once the graph grows to hold code read by its syntax or not read at all

arms.name: M-REACH-TYPED-IMPLICIT-TEXT
arms.note: code read through its facts is taken to convert nothing to a string without a call the graph holds

arms.name: M-REACH-TYPED-IMPLICIT-ITER
arms.note: code read through its facts is taken to iterate nothing without a call the graph holds

arms.name: M-REACH-ITERABLE-RETURNS
arms.note: (precision) the element an iterator's `next` returns is iterated in turn, so an iterator of a type the index does not declare runs any `next`

arms.name: M-FACTS-THROW-TEXT
arms.note: a thrown value is recorded as converted to no string, though the exception wrapping hands it to `Std.string`

arms.name: M-SITES-THROW-TEXT
arms.note: a `throw` is no string-conversion site of what it throws

arms.name: M-FACTS-ABSTRACT-CTOR-NAME
arms.note: a call of an abstract's constructor names `_new`, which no type the graph holds declares, so every `new` of an abstract is an unresolved dispatch

arms.name: M-FACTS-TEXT-LITERAL-FLAGS
arms.note: a regular expression written with flags is no construction the text writes: the compiler's position of it leaves them out, so openfl's `TextField` is not its text

arms.name: M-FACTS-HANDS
arms.note: an argument handed to target code is recorded nowhere, so a value an extern keeps never escapes

arms.name: M-FACTS-GENS
arms.note: the instantiation of a generic method is recorded nowhere, so what its type parameters stand for is never known

arms.name: M-FACTS-STRING-EXACT
arms.note: no converted value is an object of exactly its own class, so a fresh one runs the conversion of whatever its type may hold

arms.name: M-FACTS-EXACT-WRITTEN
arms.note: a local initialized with a construction is taken to hold it even after it is written again

arms.name: M-FACTS-THROW-EXCEPTION
arms.note: a thrown exception of exactly its class is recorded as converted to a string, though the wrapping throws it as it is

arms.name: M-FACTS-ALIAS-TYPEDEF
arms.note: an import alias, which no module lists, gets no record, so a type naming it names no type the table holds

arms.name: M-FACTS-STATICS-TYPEDEF
arms.note: the typedef of an enum's statics is printed with arguments after its name (`Enum<pack.E><?>`), which the type grammar does not read

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-TRUTH-FACTS
arms.note: under the truth the escapes are still read off the project's syntax, which counts every value handed to library code as escaped

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-REFLECTION-INLINED
arms.note: any reflective body spliced in is taken to produce a class from a name it lost, so the escapes are never known

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-FLOW
arms.note: a value flowing into a catch-all, a type parameter, a structure or through a cast is taken to stay in the type system

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-HANDED
arms.find: for (h in n.handed) if (!typeParameter(h.to) && !escape(h.from)) return false;
arms.note: a value handed to target code is taken to stay in the type system

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-CLOSURE
arms.note: the receiver of a method read as a value is taken to stay in the type system, though the bound function carries it

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-DYNAMIC-RECEIVER
arms.note: the receiver of a field reached by name in untyped code is taken to stay in the type system, though any of its fields may be read

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-PRODUCED
arms.note: a class a class-value producer names is taken never to be instantiated untyped

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-INSTANCES
arms.find: if (fact != null && fact.params.length == args.length) for (i => name in fact.params) bind('$id.$name', args[i]);
arms.note: a type written with arguments binds nothing, so a value a generic class lets go is of no type

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-PARAMETER
arms.find: if (bound != null) for (x in bound) if (!escapeType(x)) return false;
arms.note: a value of a type parameter is taken to be of no type, so what its instantiations bind it to never escapes

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-GENERIC-METHOD
arms.note: the instantiation of a generic method binds nothing, so a value it lets go is of no type

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-EXTENDS-EXTERN
arms.note: an instance of a class extending an extern is taken to stay in the type system, though target code runs with it as `this`

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-FIELDS
arms.find: for (f in currentFact.fields) if (f.kinds.exists(k -> k.startsWith('var(')) && !within(f.types, currentBound)) return false;
arms.note: what an escaped object's variables hold is taken to stay in the type system

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-ENUM
arms.find: case 'enum': fact.constructors.foreach(c -> constructorEscapes(id, c.name, c.type, bound));
arms.note: what an escaped enum value's constructor arguments hold is taken to stay in the type system

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-STRUCTURE
arms.note: what an escaped structure's fields hold is taken to stay in the type system

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-PLACE-ARGS
arms.note: a place of a nominal type is taken to keep the type of what it holds whatever its arguments, `Array<Dynamic>` included

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-TYPE-ARGS
arms.note: what an escaped container holds by its type arguments, which no variable of it declares, is taken to stay in the type system

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-SUBTYPES
arms.note: an escaped value is taken to be of exactly its static class, never one of its subtypes

arms.name: M-REACH-EXACT-SITE
arms.find: at.exact ? exactTypes(g, t) : runtimeTypes(g, t, at.family)
arms.note: an object built right at a conversion site may be any subtype of its class, or any escaped instance

arms.name: M-FACTS-VIEW-EXACT
arms.note: the exactness the facts record of a converted operand is dropped

arms.name: M-FACTS-VIEW-EXACT-CONVERSION
arms.note: the exactness the facts record of the argument of a conversion call is dropped

arms.name: M-FACTS-FLOW-EXACT
arms.note: the exactness of a value flowing whole is recorded nowhere

arms.name: M-FACTS-TEXT-JOINED-CONVERSION
arms.note: a conversion the compiler writes of a field read it placed across an inlined body and the text is no text's (TM's `drill.Node.parse`)

arms.name: M-FACTS-TEXT-JOINED-PLACED
arms.note: the value a field read the compiler placed across an inlined body and the text flows as is no text's (TM's `drill.Node.parse`)

arms.name: M-FACTS-TREE-OPTIONAL
arms.note: a lone `?` argument is read as an optional argument, so an unknown argument type reads as a malformed type

arms.name: M-REACH-CALLEE-WALK
arms.note: what a shared collection's region calls is admitted unwalked, so a callee growing any array proves

arms.name: M-REACH-CALLEE-REFUSED
arms.note: every call a shared collection's region makes is a culprit again, so a region calling a pure project function is refused

arms.name: M-REACH-CALLEE-BENIGN-EDGE
arms.note: a callee's push onto a fresh local of its own is followed into the built-in array type, whose body-less mutator refuses

arms.name: M-REACH-CALLEE-REWRITTEN
arms.note: a callee a build macro may rewrite is read as its source

arms.name: M-REACH-CALLEE-AMBIGUOUS
arms.note: a callee whose type name two declarations share is read as one of them

arms.name: M-REACH-CALLEE-OVERRIDES
arms.note: a dispatch on a library type reaches only the declaration, not the overrides library code declares

arms.name: M-REACH-COMPOUND-WRITE-ALIAS
arms.find: final replacing: Bool = write.kind == shape.assignKind || write.kind == shape.nullCoalAssignKind;
arms.replace:
final replacing: Bool = true;
		if (write.kind != shape.assignKind) return true;
arms.note: only a plain assignment of a shared value is an escape, so `x ??= shared` leaves `x` a fresh local whose push is taken as harmless

arms.name: M-REACH-ASSIGNMENT-VALUE-ALIAS
arms.replace: if (true) return holder.kind != shape.exprStatementKind || valueDiscarded(lineage, at - 1);
arms.note: an assignment used as a value keeps its target fresh, so `all = xs = [1]` leaves `xs` unshared though `all` holds it

arms.name: M-REACH-LAST-STATEMENT-VALUE
arms.replace: final climbs: Bool = true || kind == shape.blockStmtKind
arms.note: every construct a statement ends is climbed as if its value were discarded, so `all = { xs = [1]; }` keeps `xs` unshared

arms.name: M-REACH-DISCARDED-BODY
arms.note: a loop's body is not taken as discarding its last statement's value, so a fresh write ending a loop body makes the local shared

arms.name: M-REACH-DISCARDED-STATEMENT-BRANCH
arms.note: no statement branch or nested block is climbed, so a fresh write ending an `if` / `switch` statement branch makes the local shared

arms.name: M-ORACLE-PARALLEL-HALF-THE-CORES
arms.note: the compile budget is half the cores again, so a thirteen-configuration project compiles in four waves on a sixteen-core machine

arms.name: M-RUNMEMO-PROBE-RECOMPILES
arms.find: final held: Array<Null<HaxeRun>> = [for (i in 0...asked.length) memo?.run(asked[i], true, before[i])];
arms.note: the coverage probe compiles the tree its baseline just compiled with -v, paying a second compile per configuration

arms.name: M-RUNMEMO-KEY-IGNORES-CONTENT
arms.note: a remembered verdict answers for any content of the tree, so an edit that breaks the build is judged by the verdict of the tree before it

arms.name: M-RUNMEMO-QUOTES-THE-VERBOSE-STREAMS
arms.find: final retried: Array<Int> = verbose ? [for (k in 0...compiled.length) if (answered(runs[k]) && runs[k].status != 0) k] : [];
arms.note: a failing -v baseline is quoted with its -v lines, so a rejection's text names every parsed file

arms.name: M-RUNMEMO-FILES-A-MOVED-INPUT
arms.note: a compile whose input changed while it ran is filed under the content it started from, so that content is later answered with a verdict about another

arms.name: M-RUNMEMO-NO-BASELINE-AHEAD
arms.note: the facts compile no longer brings the baseline along, so the baseline asked next is a compile of its own

arms.name: M-PENDING-RUNS-IN-FOREGROUND
arms.find: final answer: Array<HaxeRun> = pid == null ? HaxeSpawn.runAll(_jobs, _maxBuffer, _parallel) : collect(pid);
arms.note: a background batch is run again in the foreground when it is awaited, so nothing it did while the caller worked is saved

arms.name: M-PENDING-CANCEL-LEAVES-JOBS
arms.note: a cancelled batch leaves its driver running, so the jobs it started run to their end after the run abandoned them

arms.name: M-RUNMEMO-NOT-ATTACHED
arms.find: return OracleRunMemo.attach(prepared.oracles, new OracleRunMemo(persisted, () -> [for (f in files) f.file]));
arms.note: a lint run's configurations carry no memo, so every phase compiles the tree it asks about again

arms.name: M-FACTS-NEVER-EARLY
arms.note: no run starts its facts compiles ahead, so they follow the first check that asks instead of overlapping the checks

arms.name: M-FACTS-EARLY-DIRS-LEFT
arms.note: facts compiles no check asked for leave their probe directories behind

arms.name: M-RUNMEMO-WRITTEN-UNHASHED
arms.note: the run's fingerprint rests on the library directories hashed earlier in the process, so an edit to a project whose sources arrive through -lib leaves it unchanged and the verification is answered from the baseline

arms.name: M-RUNMEMO-TRUSTS-UNSEEN-SOURCES
arms.note: a configuration that reads files outside every directory its fingerprint walks is answered from the memo, so an edit there reuses a verdict about the old content

arms.name: M-PENDING-JOBS-FILE-KEPT
arms.note: the driver leaves the job list in its directory, so a run killed mid-batch leaves the job list behind

arms.name: M-DSN-UNSEEN-DROPPED
arms.note: no narrowing is ever marked invisible to the compiler, so dead-safe-nav rewrites a Bool-local / alias / `?.`-comparison proof to `.` under null-safety and the build breaks

arms.name: M-DSN-UNSEEN-ALL
arms.note: a direct `== null` / `!= null` guard counts as invisible too, so dead-safe-nav declines the fix the compiler would accept

arms.name: M-DSN-NULLSAFE-ALWAYS
arms.note: plain code is treated as null-checked, so a runtime-sound Bool-local proof loses its fix where nothing typechecks it

arms.name: M-DSN-JOIN-EITHER
arms.note: a join forgets that one arm proved the name only invisibly, so the fix lands on a path the compiler never narrowed

arms.name: M-DSN-RENARROW-HIDES
arms.note: an invisible re-narrowing hides a proof the compiler already has, so an accepted fix is declined

arms.name: M-DSN-ASSIGN-KEEPS-UNSEEN
arms.note: a non-null assignment no longer makes the proof visible, so the fix after `x = new T()` is declined

arms.name: M-DSN-MACRO-BLIND
arms.note: a project-wide `--macro nullSafety` in the oracle hxml is ignored, so a meta-free module gets the `.` rewrite its build rejects

arms.name: M-DSN-HXML-ALWAYS-ON
arms.note: every oracle build reads as enabling null-safety, so a plain project loses the runtime-sound fix

arms.name: M-DSN-HXML-COMMENT-READ
arms.note: a commented-out `#--macro nullSafety` is read as live, so the fix is declined in a plain build

arms.name: M-DSN-HXML-LIB-PLAIN
arms.note: a `-lib` is taken as plain although its extraParams may add `@:nullSafety`, so the build-breaking fix lands

arms.name: M-DSN-HXML-INCLUDE-SKIPPED
arms.note: an included hxml is never read, so a `nullSafety` macro in it goes unseen and the build-breaking fix lands

arms.name: M-DSN-HXML-UNREADABLE-PLAIN
arms.note: an oracle hxml not generated yet reads as plain, so the fix lands before the build that may reject it exists

arms.name: M-DSN-TRY-KEEPS-ALL
arms.note: a proof made inside a `try` stays visible past it, so the `.` rewrite after the try does not compile

arms.name: M-DSN-TRY-HIDES-ALL
arms.find: final kept: Array<String> = visibleUnwritten(state, node, ctx);
arms.note: a proof made before a `try` is hidden past it, so an accepted fix is declined

arms.name: M-DSN-LONE-ARM-KEEPS-BODY
arms.note: what the body of a lone surviving `if` arm proved stays visible past the `if`, so the `.` rewrite does not compile

arms.name: M-DSN-LONE-ARM-HIDES-ALL
arms.find: final elseKept: Array<String> = elseArm == null ? visibleIn(elseState) : visibleUnwritten(elseState, elseArm, ctx);
arms.note: the condition's own narrowing is hidden past a lone surviving arm, so the fix after `if (x == null || b) return;`-style guards is declined

arms.name: M-DSN-JOIN-HIDES-ALL
arms.note: every join hides its proof, so two live arms that each narrow visibly lose their fix

arms.name: M-DSN-LONE-BRANCH-KEEPS-BODY
arms.note: what a lone live `switch` branch proved stays visible past the switch, so the `.` rewrite does not compile

arms.name: M-DSN-OWNS-NONE
arms.note: no construct keeps what its children proved, so an assignment inside a call argument loses a fix the compiler accepts

arms.name: M-NULLFLOW-BINDER-BLIND
arms.find: final bound: Array<String> = ctx.selfScopeDeclKinds.contains(kind) ? boundNames(node, ctx) : [];
arms.note: a loop binder no longer shadows the outer name, so the outer non-null proof reaches `x?.f` on the binder and the fix / dead-fallback deletion crashes at runtime on a null element

arms.name: M-NULLFLOW-CHILD-BINDER-BLIND
arms.note: a key-value loop's VALUE binder no longer shadows, so `for (k => x in m)` inherits the outer `x` proof

arms.name: M-NULLFLOW-CASE-BINDER-BLIND
arms.note: a case capture no longer shadows, so `case x:` / `case var x:` inherit the outer proof

arms.name: M-NULLFLOW-CATCH-BINDER-BLIND
arms.note: a catch variable no longer shadows, so `catch (x:Dynamic)` inherits the outer proof

arms.name: M-NULLFLOW-SHADOW-NO-RESTORE
arms.note: the outer fact is never restored past a shadowing scope, so the fix after the loop is lost

arms.name: M-NULLFLOW-SHADOW-RESTORES-WRITTEN
arms.note: the outer fact is restored even when the construct writes the name, so a null written by the iterable is read as non-null

arms.name: M-NULLITY-ALIAS-TRUSTED
arms.note: a typedef proves non-null by being one, so `typedef MaybeR = Null<R>` reads as a plain nominal again

arms.name: M-NULLITY-UNDERLYING-TRUSTED
arms.replace: if (_nominalKinds.contains(t.kind) || t.isAnonStruct || t.underlyingRaw != null) return NonNull;
arms.note: an abstract proves non-null whatever it wraps, so one over `Null<R>` is trusted

arms.name: M-NULLITY-TYPE-PARAMS-IGNORED
arms.find: if (head == null || hops > MAX_HOPS || typeParams.contains(head)) return Unproven;
arms.replace: if (head == null || hops > MAX_HOPS) return Unproven;
arms.note: a type parameter resolves to whatever same-named type is in scope, so `m<R>(x:R)` borrows class `R`'s proof

arms.name: M-NULLITY-UNRESOLVED-PROVEN
arms.note: a name that resolves to nothing is proven by the empty agreement

arms.name: M-NULLITY-GUARD-IGNORED
arms.note: a `#if`-guarded declaration answers for every branch, though the index kept only one

arms.name: M-NULLITY-HOPS-CUT
arms.note: no alias or underlying type is followed, so an alias of a class or an abstract over one proves nothing

arms.name: M-NULLITY-ANON-REFUSED
arms.note: an anonymous-structure typedef proves nothing, though a structure value is non-null under null safety

arms.name: M-NULLITY-SCOPE-LOST
